quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting a freeway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a freeway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines may be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What happens if you park illegally in a disabled parking spot?

options.text: No consequences.
Only a fine.
Fines and possible jail time.
Fines, possible jail time, loss of driving privileges, and/or car impoundment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fines, possible jail time, loss of driving privileges, and/or car impoundment.
questions.explanation: Parking illegally in a disabled spot results in a fine of $350 to $5,000, possible jail time, loss of driving privileges, and/or car impoundment. Fines may be doubled for illegal use of disabled plates or placards.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely or if there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert other drivers if you lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always yield to other vehicles when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What happens when a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: It is allowed because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They always receive a warning.
Their bicycle will be impounded.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers. Both motorists and bicyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Dashed white lines may be crossed to pass if safe. Yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection and the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be prepared to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You are less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, worsens your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid all bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your following distance because it takes longer to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming traffic.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you see a car with bright headlights coming toward you, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Don't drink if you are going to drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road that:

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
Is directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without moving your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually makes the driver react more slowly to hazards.
Usually makes the driver go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually makes the driver react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react more slowly to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or frightening it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers to keep right to avoid an upcoming hazard.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, you should look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left at which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light.
A flashing yellow light.
A green arrow pointing left.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left.
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you can turn left safely. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them in retaliation.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and try to get away from the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: When you approach an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on your driving and watch for people on or near the road.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so that driver can see you.
